newsitem.title: UK: Frontline sees continued tanker rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Frontline sees continued tanker rate rises.

text.p: Frontline Ltd said on Friday it was confident that rates for large tankers would continue their strong recent rises, driven by increasing oil consumption in Asia and a limited orderbook for new vessels.
The Bermuda-based tanker owner added that it believed rates for large Capesize bulk carriers would also start steadily improving from their current lows.

"It is the directors opinion that a moderate order book for large tanker tonnage and an increase in the consumption of petroleum in Asia provide a good basis for a positive rate development in the coming period," Frontline said.
Commenting on its first half results, the Oslo-listed company said that developments so far in the third quarter confirmed the trend.
Results would also be helped by cost reductions linked to its move from Sweden to Bermuda.
"Based on these observations, the directors expects a significant improvement in results for the third quarter," Frontline said.
Frontline earlier said it made net profit of $1.7 million in the first half against a net loss a year earlier of $6.1 million.
Frontline operates a fleet of large Suezmax and VLCC tankers as well as a number of Ore/Bulk/Oil vessels which it said have been mainly carrying oil due to low bulk freight rates.
"The large number of orders for Capesize vessel has now been considerable depleted through deliveries, and this is expected to result in a gradual improvement in the market," Frontline said.

However, the company said it was not satisfied with earnings from its VLCCs during the first half, and was working to remedy the situation. "Shareholders should be able to anticipate a significant improvement in the third quarter," it said.

As part of its plans to improve earnings, a contract has been signed with an unnamed Asian oil firm. "This agreement will secure continuous employment for approximately 1.5 VLCC for the next 12 months," Frontline said.
Measure to cut costs have accelerated since its move from Sweden. The original plan to save $12 million per year is being implemented without significant problems, the company said.
Frontline added: "Following the replacement of the crew and management of Front Breaker on July 16, the operating expenses for all the company's wholly-owned ships are now at a competitive level."

In addition a further $3 million will be saved each year through the renegotiation of insurance and finance contracts, Frontline said. -Julian Bray, Reuters Shipping News +44 171 542 4087/4012 Fax 542 5017
